Heritage sites by state

Heritage sites in Uttarakhand: Jageshwar, Kalsi and Himalayan temples

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

Uttarakhand has one UNESCO listing, the Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks, a natural site. Its cultural heritage includes Ashoka's rock edict at Kalsi, the stone temple clusters of Jageshwar and Baijnath, the Katarmal sun temple, painted rock shelters at Lakhudiyar, the early brick temple at Jagatgram and the Char Dham shrines.

We build Uttarakhand study tours linking the Kalsi edict with the Kumaon temples, and run a Brahmi workshop for groups before they travel.

Uttarakhand's heritage beyond pilgrimage

Uttarakhand is best known for the pilgrimage routes to Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri and Yamunotri, but its archaeology runs much deeper. Painted rock shelters in Kumaon, an Ashokan edict in the Doon valley, a 3rd century horse sacrifice site at Jagatgram and hundreds of stone temples from the Katyuri and Chand periods show a long history of settlement and trade between the plains and Tibet.

The state has two historic regions, Garhwal in the west and Kumaon in the east, each with its own dynasties, dialects and building traditions, including the timber and stone kath-kuni houses of the upper valleys. For the wider temple story, see our explainer on Indian temple architecture.

Kalsi, Jagatgram and early history

At Kalsi, near the meeting of the Yamuna and Tons rivers, a large quartz boulder carries a full set of Ashoka's major rock edicts, including the thirteenth edict on the Kalinga war. An elephant is incised on one face with the word 'gajatame'. It is one of the northernmost Ashokan edicts and is protected by the ASI. Our Brahmi workshop teaches students to read the script used here.

Nearby at Jagatgram (Barwala), excavation exposed brick altars associated with ashvamedha sacrifices performed by a local king, Shilavarman, of about the 3rd century CE, recorded on inscribed bricks. Govishan near Kashipur and Virabhadra near Rishikesh are other excavated early historic sites.

Ancient temples in Kumaon and Garhwal

Jageshwar, in a deodar forest near Almora, has more than a hundred stone temples built from about the 7th to the 12th or 13th centuries, most in the Nagara style with curved towers capped by wooden canopies. Baijnath, near Garur, is another Katyuri-period group beside the Gomati river. The Katarmal sun temple, on a hill near Almora, is a 13th century complex whose carved wooden doors are now in the National Museum in New Delhi.

In Garhwal, the temples of Lakhamandal, Adi Badri and Pandukeshwar, and the great shrines of Kedarnath and Badrinath, continue the tradition. Our lecture Nagara temple architecture is the best preparation for these mountain temples, which adapt the plains style to snow and timber.

Rock art and Himalayan landscapes

Lakhudiyar, on the Almora to Barechina road, means 'a lakh caves'. Its rock shelter has paintings in red, black and white of human figures in lines, animals and wavy patterns. The dating is uncertain, with estimates ranging widely, so it is best described as prehistoric to early historic. Our programme Rock art of India explains how such paintings are recorded and dated.

The Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks were inscribed as a natural World Heritage Site in 1988 and extended in 2005. They are valued for their alpine meadows and high mountain ecology, though the area is also part of the sacred geography of the Nanda Devi Raj Jat pilgrimage.

Planning a heritage trip to Uttarakhand

Distances in the hills are longer than they look on the map. Dehradun is a good base for Kalsi and Lakhamandal, and Almora for Jageshwar, Katarmal and Lakhudiyar. March to June and September to November are the best seasons, and the Char Dham shrines close in winter.

Questions people ask

Are there UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Uttarakhand?

Yes, one: the Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks, a natural site inscribed in 1988 and extended in 2005. Uttarakhand has no cultural World Heritage Site.

What is the Kalsi rock edict?

Kalsi, near Dehradun, has a large boulder inscribed with Ashoka's major rock edicts in Brahmi, including the edict about the Kalinga war. An elephant is incised on one face. It is one of the northernmost of Ashoka's major rock edicts.

Which are the oldest temples in Uttarakhand?

The temple groups of Jageshwar, Baijnath and Lakhamandal include some of the oldest, with buildings from about the 7th century onward. The brick altars at Jagatgram are older still, but they are sacrificial altars rather than temples.

Where can you see rock paintings in Uttarakhand?

Lakhudiyar, near Almora, is the best known painted rock shelter, with red, black and white figures of people, animals and patterns. Other shelters are known in Kumaon. Check access locally, as some are on steep slopes.
